messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics Coupled to Nanoelectrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry (DMF-nESI-MS) for Dried Blood Spot (DBS) Succinylacetone (SA) Quantification

REAGENTS USED:
  - Dried Blood Spot Punch (3.2 mm diameter filter-paper punch bearing dried whole blood, fortified with 13C5-SA internal standard)
  - Methanol (neat MeOH, pre-extraction solvent, 15 uL droplets)
  - SA Extraction/Derivatization/MS Reagent (6.5 mM hydrazine and 15 uM 13C5-SA in 80:20 acetonitrile:DI water with 0.1% v/v formic acid, 15 uL droplets)

STEPS:
1-2. Pre-extraction wash 1: Load a 15 uL methanol droplet, actuate onto the DBS punch, incubate 15 min at room temperature, then actuate the droplet away from the punch to a waste reservoir.
3-4. Pre-extraction wash 2: Repeat the load/incubate/waste-removal cycle a second time.
5-6. Pre-extraction wash 3: Repeat the load/incubate/waste-removal cycle a third time.
7. First Derivatization Step: Load a fresh 15 uL droplet of the hydrazine/13C5-SA/acetonitrile:water solvent, actuate onto the residual (methanol-washed) DBS punch, and incubate 15 min at 37 C on a hot-plate until the droplet evaporates.
8. Second Derivatization Step: Load a second fresh 15 uL droplet of the same hydrazine reagent, deliver it to the residual blood spot, and incubate for 1 min at room temperature (with circular actuation around the punch).
9. Detection: Actuate the derivatized droplet to the inlet of a pulled-glass capillary nanoESI emitter positioned near the mass spectrometer orifice; apply a DC potential to generate a stable nanoelectrospray and acquire MS/MS spectra, quantifying succinylacetone from the m/z 155->137 (SA) product-ion intensity relative to the m/z 160->142 (13C5-SA internal standard) product-ion intensity; then discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful SA quantification is confirmed by a linear calibration curve (peak-intensity ratio of derivatized SA to derivatized 13C5-SA internal standard vs. spiked SA concentration) with good linearity, an extraction efficiency comparable to conventional manual/robotic extraction methods, and measured DBS punch concentrations statistically indistinguishable from those obtained by the standard newborn-screening technique, supporting use of the method for hepatorenal tyrosinemia (HT) screening.

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's automated nine-step DBS sample-processing procedure (Experimental Section, 'DMF-Driven DBS Processing and Analysis'), covering the triplicate methanol pre-extraction wash (steps 1-6), the two-part hydrazine extraction/derivatization (steps 7-8), and delivery to the capillary emitter for nESI-MS/MS quantification (step 9), as depicted in Figure 3. Incubation durations, temperatures, and droplet volumes (15 uL per droplet, 15 min RT washes, 15 min at 37C derivatization) are taken directly from the Experimental section. Because BioScript has no primitive for a persistent solid substrate (the DBS punch itself remains on-chip across all nine steps while droplets are cycled past it), the punch is modeled by re-dispensing the 'dbs_sample' manifest before each wash/derivatization step rather than reusing a single droplet handle, consistent with how repeated reagents (e.g., enzyme) are re-dispensed in other translated protocols. Likewise, because the paper's detection modality is nanoESI-MS/MS (not a fluorogenic readout), the 'detect fluorescence' primitive is used as a stand-in for the generic detect-and-quantify step, representing the SA/13C5-SA product-ion intensity ratio rather than an actual fluorescence signal, since BioScript's grammar does not expose a dedicated mass-spectrometry detect module. The paper's impedance-based feedback control system (Figure 2, automated voltage step-up on movement failure), the physical capillary-emitter insertion/alignment into the DMF device, the tip-washing/rinse-efficiency experiment (Figure 5), the dual-emitter amino-acid + SA parallel workflow (Figure 6), and the head-to-head statistical comparison against the standard NSO technique (Table 2) are hardware-control, validation, or comparison sub-experiments with no corresponding BioScript primitive, and are intentionally not modeled; only the core nine-step SA extraction/derivatization/detection protocol is captured here.

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper's DBS punch is a single physical object that remains on-chip for the full nine-step procedure; BioScript has no persistent-substrate primitive, so the punch is modeled as a fresh 'dispense dbs_sample' at each step rather than one droplet reused across mixes.

Detection in the paper is nanoESI-MS/MS (parent ion m/z 155->137 for SA, 160->142 for 13C5-SA), not a fluorogenic assay. 'fluorescence' is used here only because it is the sole detect module exposed by BioScript's grammar; it stands in for a generic quantitative signal read, not an actual fluorescence measurement.

The paper describes the Step 8 droplet being actuated around five electrodes adjacent to the DBS in a circular fashion during the 1 min incubation. BioScript has no primitive for spatial actuation patterns, so this is folded into a plain 'mix ... for 60s' with no positional detail.
